interpretation.fragment.concentration.hi: {dominant_n} of the {total_n} cases ({dominant_share_pct}%) come from postal code {dominant_label}, pointing to strong place-based clustering.
interpretation.fragment.concentration.mo: {dominant_n} of the {total_n} cases ({dominant_share_pct}%) come from postal code {dominant_label}, a moderate concentration.
interpretation.fragment.concentration.di: Cases are spread across several postal-code areas; the area with the most cases, postal code {dominant_label}, accounts for only {dominant_share_pct}% of the cluster.
interpretation.fragment.denominator.risi: Test volume rose from {test_first} to {test_last} tests per week, while positivity stayed nearly flat ({positivity_first_pct}% to {positivity_last_pct}%). Part of the rise is therefore attributable to test volume, not incidence.
Positivity rose from {positivity_first_pct}% to {positivity_last_pct}% at a comparable test volume. The rise is therefore not attributable to test volume.
interpretation.fragment.denominator.stab: Test volume and positivity are stable over the shown period ({positivity_first_pct}% to {positivity_last_pct}%).
interpretation.fragment.demography.shift: The age distribution has shifted towards the {dominant_band} group, against a baseline of {baseline_band}.
interpretation.fragment.completeness.war: Note: the last {incomplete_days_phrase} are incomplete due to reporting delay. The true count is likely higher.
interpretation.fragment.recommendation.r: This is a pathogen on the curated trigger list; assess promptly and check the statutory notification duty.
interpretation.fragment.recommendation.h: The combination of size and concentration warrants considering classification as a (possible) epidemic and coordination with infection prevention or public health.
interpretation.fragment.recommendation.m: Monitor this cluster's development; a classification of cluster without epidemic may be appropriate as long as no further signs of spread emerge.
interpretation.fragment.recommendation.d: Assess this cluster on the basis of the data above; there is not yet sufficient evidence for urgent follow-up.

info.title: Info
info.intro: Background on EpiSODIC's detection algorithms, cluster states and access model.
info.algorithms.title: Detection algorithms
info.algorithms.note: A cluster can be detected by more than one algorithm at once; see "detected by" on the dossier.
info.algorithms.col.name: Name
info.algorithms.farrington: Compares the observed weekly case count against an expectation built from historical data (surveillance::farringtonFlexible). Signals when the observed count exceeds the computed threshold; needs sufficient baseline history to run at all.
info.algorithms.same_place: Signals when n or more cases of the same pathogen occur at the same place within k days. Runs at ward level inside hospitals; at institution level everywhere else (long-term care, out-of-hours service, general practice). Needs no baseline.
info.algorithms.rare_trigger: For a fixed list of rare-but-serious pathogens, a single reported case is notable on its own; a baseline model would only produce silence here. Signals immediately once the configured minimum is reached, regardless of baseline.
info.algorithms.mem: For pathogens with a genuine season (influenza, RSV), fits pre- and post-epidemic thresholds from earlier fully observed seasons using the Moving Epidemic Method (mem::memmodel), and signals when the last complete week crosses the start threshold. It answers a different question from Farrington: not "is this week higher than expected" but "has the epidemic begun". Runs at region level only, and its thresholds are drawn on the Pathogen screen.
info.states.title: Cluster states
info.states.new: Just detected, not yet assessed by anyone.
info.states.assessing: Under assessment; an epidemiologist is classifying the cluster.
info.states.monitoring: Assessed and actively tracked; no reason yet to close it.
info.states.closable: Signals have subsided enough to close, awaiting confirmation.
info.states.reassess: Previously closed, but grown again past the threshold; needs reassessment.
info.states.closed: Closed by an epidemiologist, or automatically by the system after a period with no new cases.
info.access.title: Access
info.access.body: Reading is anonymous: anyone who reaches the app can view clusters, streams and the archive without signing in. Signing in is only needed to classify a cluster, close it, or mute a stream - every write is attributed to the signed-in user.
interpretation.fragment.curve_shape.poin: All cases fall within a single maximum incubation period, pointing to a point source: a shared exposure around one moment, rather than person-to-person spread.
interpretation.fragment.curve_shape.prop: Cases span considerably more than one maximum incubation period, pointing to person-to-person spread rather than a single shared exposure.
interpretation.fragment.curve_shape.ambi: The spread of cases over time does not clearly fit either a point source or person-to-person spread; further investigation of the exposure is needed to distinguish between them.

panel.rt.unavailable.no_serial_interval: Rt cannot be computed: this pathogen's configuration is missing a serial interval (si_mean_days/si_sd_days).
panel.rt.unavailable.epiestim_missing: Rt cannot be computed: the 'EpiEstim' R package is not installed.
panel.rt.unavailable.insufficient_histor: Not enough case history in this cluster yet to compute Rt.

report.note_versioned: This is an automated, version-bound report. Every new render gets its own version number; this copy stays unchanged after it is sent.
report.rt_note: Time-varying *effective* reproduction number, not R0 - computed over 7-day rolling windows with [EpiEstim](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=EpiEstim). Windows within the still-incomplete reporting period are omitted.
report.footer: Generated by EpiSODIC. This document holds no live link to the application; all data is frozen at the moment of rendering.
pathogen.title: Pathogen activity
pathogen.note: One pathogen across the whole catchment, over a period you choose. This is the epidemiological view: where a season stands against its own history, how fast transmission is running region-wide, and which signals were raised while it ran. The Clusters screen answers what to do today; this one answers what is going on.
pathogen.empty: No case data has been loaded yet, so there is nothing to describe.
pathogen.showing: Showing {from} to {to} · case data current as of {asof}
pathogen.panel.curve.title: Weekly incidence
pathogen.panel.curve.empty: No cases of this pathogen in the selected period.
pathogen.panel.curve.note: Confirmed cases per week across the whole catchment. Weeks still filling up are drawn faded, so the tail is not read as a decline.
pathogen.panel.curve.mem_note: Moving Epidemic Method thresholds, fitted on the {seasons} fully observed seasons before this one and never on this one: epidemic start at {pre} and end at {post} cases per week. Crossing the start threshold is what the mem detector fires on.
pathogen.panel.curve.mem_unavailable: This pathogen is treated as seasonal, but there are not yet two fully observed earlier seasons to fit thresholds on, so none are drawn.
pathogen.panel.overlay.title: Against earlier years
pathogen.panel.overlay.empty: Only one period has data, so there is nothing to compare against yet.
pathogen.panel.overlay.note: Every period's curve on one axis, the selected one drawn heavier. Read it for shape as much as height: an ordinary-sized peak arriving six weeks early is its own finding.
pathogen.panel.rt.title: Effective reproduction number (Rt), catchment-wide
pathogen.panel.rt.note: Rt over 7-day sliding windows, estimated on the pathogen's whole incidence rather than on any one cluster's - which is the population the renewal model assumes it is seeing. Conditioned on case history from before the selected period, so the opening weeks are not inflated by the series simply starting there.
pathogen.panel.rt.not_applicable: Rt is not computed for this pathogen: its configuration does not mark it as one where person-to-person transmission is what the case count reflects.
pathogen.panel.denominator.note: Tests and positivity across the catchment for this pathogen. A rise in cases with flat positivity is a testing effect; a rise in both is not.
pathogen.panel.demography.note: Median age this period is {median}, against {baseline} for this pathogen outside it. A shifting age distribution often changes before counts do.
pathogen.panel.care_line.title: Where cases were found
pathogen.panel.care_line.note: Primary versus secondary care tells you whether you are looking at community circulation or at what reached hospital.
